newsitem.title: JAPAN: Suzuki says Hungary a possible Euro deal.
newsitem.headline: Suzuki says Hungary a possible Euro deal.

text.p: Suzuki Motor Corp sees its Hungarian unit as a candidate for possible joint car production with General Motors Corp in Europe.

"(Our) Hungarian unit is a candidate (for a car project in Europe). But we don't know yet whether to do (the project) with building a new plant or using other sites," a Suzuki vice president Yoshio Saito told reporters on Tuesday.
On November 1, General Motors International Operations said it and Suzuki were exploring possible cooperation in the small car segment in Europe.
Suzuki's Hungarian unit Magyar Suzuki Corp produces Swift cars.
The cooperation is likely to be a joint development and a joint production for marketing small cars in Europe under both carmakers' brands, Saito said.

Suzuki, owned 3.2 percent by GM, earlier said its parent current profit rose 2.9 percent from a year earlier to 10.59 billion yen in the first-half period, surpassing the previous 10.29 billion yen in the first half of 1995/96.
